newsitem.title: USA: NJ gov says filed tobacco suits to show claims.
newsitem.headline: NJ gov says filed tobacco suits to show claims.

text.p: New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman on Thursday said that the attorney general filed a statement of damages against two tobacco companies, Philip Morris Cos Inc, and R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co.
"The purpose of the filing is to provide all parties involved in the litigation with a sense of our claims against Phillip Morris and R.J. Reynolds," she said, in prepared remarks.
A press spokesman was not immediately available to provide more information about the state's filing.
Whitman, who said a resolution was distant, said she wanted any money to go to children and for healthcare.

"Although a decision in the case or a settlement are a long way off, it would be my preference that the first use for any monetary damages would be to fund health care for children and for uncompensated care."

The Republican governor added that in addition to getting taxpayers reimbursed by tobacco companies, she wanted to immediately stop them from targeting youngsters and ensure that adults who smoked had "full and complete" warnings about the risks.
At least 25 states have sued the tobacco industry to recop state Medicaid funds spent treating smoking-related illnesses.
